page: Microsoft Azure HB176-144rs_v4 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv4 server family. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 processors managed through the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 144 dedicated compute cores alongside 768 GB of total system memory, providing approximately 5.33 GB of RAM per allocated core. Built for tightly coupled parallel computing tasks, the instance supports Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking to facilitate low-latency node-to-node communication across large clusters.

Storage configuration includes 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD scratch space alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. The local solid-state drives offer high-capacity, low-latency temporary storage, which reduces input/output bottlenecks when handling large working datasets. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, focusing entirely on CPU-driven parallel execution. Additionally, network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, reflecting its common deployment within isolated internal cluster networks.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the provision of 144 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 768 GB of memory and expansive local NVMe capacity provides strong resource density for compute-bound workloads. By avoiding GPU hardware overhead, the platform optimizes core compute cycles and high-speed local data handling for workloads that rely purely on CPU vector math, parallel algorithmic models, computational fluid dynamics, molecular dynamics, and large-scale engineering simulations.
